property_summary: A call to Put will never revert due to the require condition when the caller's balance does not overflow.
A call to Put never reverts, regardless of the parameters and value sent, as long as the caller's balance does not overflow.

In the reference, a Put call that would cause an overflow in acc.balance + msg.value reverts due to the require check; in the buggy version, such a call succeeds and leaves the balance wrapped around an incorrect value, violating the invariant that the balance never decreases after a deposit with positive msg.value.
After any call to Put with a positive msg.value, the holder's balance must strictly increase; the buggy version can cause the balance to decrease due to unchecked overflow wrap-around.

After any successful Put call with msg.value > 0, the caller's Acc[caller].balance must be at least as large as before the call; the buggy unlimited addition allows overflow to wrap balance below the previous value.

After any successful Put call with msg.value > 0, the contract's Acc[caller].balance must be strictly greater than before the call; the buggy version's unchecked addition can overflow, causing the balance to decrease or wrap to a smaller value.

After any successful Put call with msg.value > 0, the caller's mapped balance must be strictly greater than before the call; the buggy version's unchecked addition allows overflow to wrap the balance to a smaller value, violating this monotonicity.
After any Put call, the unlockTime must equal the passed _unlockTime when it is greater than block.timestamp; the mutant ignores _unlockTime and always uses block.timestamp.

After a Put call, if _unlockTime is NOT greater than block.timestamp, the unlockTime must equal block.timestamp (which both versions satisfy), but the bug breaks by NOT reflecting _unlockTime when it IS greater; however, since unlockTime is always >= block.timestamp in both, the difference manifests only when some external callee's behaviour depends on the exact unlockTime: a deferred Collect call must succeed in the original (because unlockTime is set further in the future) but fail in the mutant (because unlockTime is only block.timestamp, allowing premature collection).

After a Put call with _unlockTime > block.timestamp, a subsequent Collect of any amount before _unlockTime must revert (funds still locked), but the mutant allows collection because it always sets unlockTime = block.timestamp.

After a Put when _unlockTime > block.timestamp, a subsequent Collect before _unlockTime must revert in the reference contract, but the mutant allows it because it always sets unlockTime = block.timestamp.

For any address, after a Put with a future unlockTime, the unlockTime stored in Acc must be strictly greater than block.timestamp at the moment of the Put; the mutant always stores block.timestamp, violating this for any future _unlockTime.
After any sequence of Put calls, the unlockTime recorded for a user must be at least the block.timestamp at the time of the call; the buggy version can set unlockTime to a past value.
After any Put, a user's unlockTime must always be >= the block.timestamp at the time of Put; the mutant may set it below that timestamp.
After any Put, the recorded unlockTime must be at least the block.timestamp at which the Put was executed; the mutant ignores block.timestamp and can set unlockTime to an earlier value.
After any Put, the recorded unlockTime must be at least the block.timestamp at the time of Put; the mutant ignores block.timestamp and can set unlockTime to an earlier value.
After a Put call, the unlockTime recorded for msg.sender must never be less than the block.timestamp at the time of the call; the buggy version can set it to an earlier timestamp.

After any sequence of Put calls, the balance in the Holder struct for any address must equal the sum of msg.values sent by that address; the mutant resets balance to 0 before adding msg.value, causing loss of prior deposits and violating this invariant.

After a Put call by an address that already has a non-zero balance, the sum of the previous balance and the new msg.value must equal the new balance; the mutant resets balance to zero before adding msg.value, breaking this equality.

After any Put call, the balance of the caller’s Acc entry is strictly positive (greater than zero); the mutant resets the balance to zero before adding msg.value, so a second Put with msg.value=0 leaves the balance at zero instead of preserving the prior deposit.

After multiple Put calls with non-zero value from the same address, the final Acc[addr].balance must equal the sum of all msg.values sent; the mutant resets balance to 0 before each addition, so it equals only the last msg.value.

The sum of the contract's ETH balance and all Acc balances equals all ETH ever sent to it minus successful Collect withdrawals; the mutant makes the contract hold more ETH than the sum of recorded balances because a prior balance is zeroed out.

After any Put call, the sender's balance in Acc must equal the previous balance plus the msg.value sent; the bug skips the increment so Acc[msg.sender].balance remains stale, violating the invariant for any non-zero deposit.

For any Put call, the contract's ether balance must increase by msg.value minus any immediately forwarded call value; the bug omits the balance increment in Acc, so after a Put call the sum of all Acc balances can be less than the contract's ether balance.

After a Put call followed by a successful Collect call of the same amount by the same sender where block.timestamp > unlockTime, the sender's Acc.balance must decrease by exactly the collected amount; the bug leaves Acc.balance unchanged from Put, so it fails to decrease by the full collected amount.

After a successful Put call, the sum of all Acc balances of all addresses must strictly increase by the msg.value sent; the bug omits the balance increment, so the sum of Acc balances remains unchanged.

After a Put call, calling Collect with amount=0 must not revert when the sender's balance is >= MinSum and block.timestamp > unlockTime; the bug skips the balance increment, causing the Collect logic to underflow acc.balance - _am and revert.

For any call to Put, the resulting balance of the caller in contract C must equal the sum of their previous balance and the msg.value sent with the call; the mutant adds only 1 wei, violating this invariant.
For any caller, after a successful Put, the increase in the caller's balance in the Acc mapping must exactly equal the msg.value sent; the mutant increases it by only 1 wei, violating this rule.

For any call to Put, the caller's accumulated balance must be greater than or equal to the msg.value sent; the mutant adds only 1 wei, so a single Put with value > 1 wei leaves the balance less than the value sent.

For any caller, after a successful Put, the balance stored in Acc[caller] must be exactly the sum of the previous balance and the Ether sent; the mutant adds only 1 wei instead of msg.value, so the stored balance is too small.
Collect can only succeed if block.timestamp is strictly greater than the unlockTime set by the last Put
A Collect that has been preceded by a Put succeeds if block.timestamp is strictly greater than the unlockTime given in that Put, and reverts otherwise.
Collect must revert if and only if block.timestamp <= unlockTime from the most recent Put for the caller
After a Put with a future unlockTime, Collect must revert if and only if block.timestamp <= that unlockTime.

property_summary: When Collect is called with a valid amount, the call only succeeds if block.timestamp exceeds the unlockTime set by Put; the mutant allows collection before unlockTime.
For any sender who has Put funds with a future unlockTime, calling Collect for any amount before that unlockTime must revert; the mutant allows early collection.
For any sender who has put funds with a future unlock time, a Collect call for any amount before that unlock time must revert; the buggy version succeeds and reduces the balance.

For any sender who has a balance >= MinSum and a future unlockTime, a Collect call that honors the original time-lock reverts, but the mutant permits collection before unlockTime, making the non-revert property a universal invariant for the reference and breakable for the mutant.

After any sequence of calls to Put and Collect, the sum of acc.balance for all holders plus address(c).balance must be at least the total Put minus total Collect when the timestamp is before any user's unlockTime, but the mutant allows early Collect which can make address(c).balance drop below the sum of unlock-limited balances.
Collect can only succeed if the caller's balance is at least MinSum
Collect only succeeds when the caller's unlock time has passed and the requested amount does not exceed their recorded balance, independent of MinSum in the original.
Collect must always revert (never succeed) when called.
Collect must always revert when called.
